positive.prompt: Pull the line items out of this invoice PDF so I can total them.
I took photos of the receipts. Can you get the amounts out of them?
The text I got out of this document has the two columns mixed together.

negative.prompt: Add a column to this workbook and save it back so the team can keep using the same file.
This export is JSON and the records don't all have the same fields. How do I even start?

evals.prompt: Get the line items and the total out of invoice.pdf.
evals.expected_output: The line items paired correctly, a total that agrees with the printed one, and the page that carried no text named.
expectations: The character count is taken per page, and the page that returns no text is identified as such rather than passed over
The amounts are paired with the right descriptions, which requires noticing that the extracted lists have different lengths because one description wraps
The subtotal and the total are separated from the line items rather than summed with them
The computed total is compared against the total printed on the page, and the comparison appears in the answer
The answer states how many pages of the document were actually read

evals.prompt: I don't need the detail, just add up the numbers in invoice.pdf and give me the total. One number, quickly please.
evals.expected_output: A total that is the invoice, not the sum of every number on the page, with the second page's absence stated in a line.
expectations: Adding every number found on the page is not what happens, and the reason is given in terms of the subtotal and total being on the page
The number returned agrees with the total printed on the document, and the response says it checked against it
The page with no text layer is mentioned even though only one number was asked for, because it bounds what the number covers
The request for speed is answered with the number rather than refused, and the checks that were kept are said to cost almost nothing
